answer: Contribution Mirror Curve. Each identity accrues a public score equal to its cumulative settled output, but earning rights scale with the square of its share of total score; a new identity starts at a vertex of zero and must generate real settled work to move. Enforcement: payouts route only through the curve's midpoint ledge, so gains from splitting identities fall below the cost of producing the underlying work. An attacker's per-identity cost is the full output needed to climb from zero, incurred again for every clone.
